about:
# Obvi Guide

A guide viewer for WoW Forever, plus the addons around it. Each folder is its own addon, released as its own
CurseForge project (except the Zygor bridge, which isn't published):

| Folder | Addon | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `ObviGuide` | Obvi Guide | The viewer. Reads guides in its own format and RestedXP's; other formats can be added by addons. Ships no guides. |
| `ObviGuide_Scribe` | Obvi Guide: Scribe | Write guides in game: record while playing, edit, test, export. |
| `ObviGuide_Dungeons` | Obvi Guide: Dungeons | Dungeon quest guides and dungeon keys. |
| `ObviGuide_Professions` | Obvi Guide: Professions | Profession leveling guides. |
| `ObviGuide_Extras` | Obvi Guide: Extras | Guides for other unlocks, such as the Aqual Quintessence and the Cozy Sleeping Bag. |
| `ObviGuide_Zygor` | Obvi Guide: Zygor | Reads the guides of your own installed Zygor addon in game, straight from Zygor's folder (it brings its own Zygor reader), so Zygor itself can stay disabled. Only the guides your Zygor licence covers. Not published anywhere: friends are welcome to it, but it isn't promoted. |

Writing guides: see [ObviGuide/docs/FORMAT.md](https://github.com/rhnorskov/obvi-guide/blob/main/ObviGuide/docs/FORMAT.md).

## QuestieDB

Obvi Guide reads quest pre-quests and quest XP from [QuestieDB](https://github.com/Questie/QuestieDB), Questie's
quest database, an addon of its own. Quest Catchup, skipping quests you can't take yet and the XP shown
need it; the rest works without it. How you get it:

- **CurseForge app:** installed with Obvi Guide (it's a required dependency of the CurseForge project).
- **The install script below:** installs and updates it too.
- **By hand:** the `QuestieDB-<version>-Forever.zip` from its [releases](https://github.com/Questie/QuestieDB/releases),
  or [QuestieDB on CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questiedb). Questie users already have it.

Obvi Guide still loads without it. It isn't bundled: it's a 15 MB addon that reads its data from its own folder, and
not all of its data is under a licence that allows passing it on.

## Trying the newest version

To play with the latest changes before they're released, paste this into PowerShell. It downloads this repo from
GitHub and puts Obvi Guide, Dungeons, Professions, Extras and the Zygor bridge in your game's AddOns folder (no git
needed), plus QuestieDB; run it again to update:

```
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhnorskov/obvi-guide/main/tools/install.ps1)))
```

It finds the game by itself; add `-Path "<game folder>\_forever_\Interface\AddOns"` if it doesn't. See
[tools/install.ps1](https://github.com/rhnorskov/obvi-guide/blob/main/tools/install.ps1) for the other options.

## Development

Link each addon folder into the game's `Interface\AddOns` (a junction per folder; the game needs each addon directly
in `AddOns`), e.g. from an elevated or developer-mode prompt:

```
mklink /J "C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\ObviGuide" "%CD%\ObviGuide"
```

Type check all addons: `powershell -File tools\check.ps1`.

Releases: push a `v*` tag. Every addon whose TOC has an `X-Curse-Project-ID` is packaged and uploaded
(`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/pkgmeta/`).

## Licence

GPL-3.0, see [LICENSE](https://github.com/rhnorskov/obvi-guide/blob/main/LICENSE).

# Obvi Guide

## v0.5.0

- WoW Forever only: retail is no longer supported.
- Waypoints (setting) has Auto, now the default: Shortest Path Forever shows the way when it's installed, else
  Obvi Guide's arrow. If you never changed the setting you get Auto; pick Obvi Guide arrow to keep the arrow.
- QuestieDB now comes with Obvi Guide in WoW Forever: the CurseForge app installs it as a required dependency, and
  `tools/install.ps1` installs and updates it.
- Auto accept and turn in work as Zygor's: only what the step you're on still has to do (no longer the next step's
  quests, nor lines hidden for you), and declining a quest leaves auto accept off for a few seconds.
- A mob two lines name shows its action key on both (Kill Kurzen Jungle Fighter [a-3] under the line it came from).
- Pressing the action key again in an NPC's quest window no longer accepts the quest shown (the game took the key as
  Accept): the key only interacts once the window is closed.
- At an open trainer, clicking a step's "Learn …" or "Train …" line trains it, and the action key that talked to the
  trainer trains the step's next one, then the next.
- A Collect line can be for a skill range (`range`): it needs only what the points left in it need. Once
  met, it stays ticked while you make things, until you run out of the item.
- A Sell line (`Sell(item, keep)`) shows items to sell: while you have more than the guide still needs, with how
  many are spare, and only if vendors buy them. At a merchant, clicking it sells the spare.
- A Collect line can say where the item is sold (`at`): clicking it shows the way to the nearest seller.
- A Collect line can be for parts still to make (`toMake`): it needs the reagents for the ones not in your bags yet.
  A Make line can make up to a count in your bags (`:CraftsUpTo`).
- A "Make …" line can name its recipe: clicking it, or its action key, opens the profession and makes what the skill
  points left in its range need. Its key shows what the next press does: "open" while the profession's window is
  closed, "make 13" once it's open.
- A step can offer several places to go (`nearest = true`, e.g. trainers in Stormwind, Ironforge and Darkshore): it
  takes you to the nearest one, picked again when you enter another zone, and shows only that one's NPC.
- The next-step arrow pulses gold while you're on an earlier step than the guide has got to (you went back); its
  tooltip says which step that is. Kept across a reload.
- The current step on the world map: its destination as a gold pin and the spots it marks ("multiple locations") as
  dots, in the minimap's colours, on the zone's map and the continent's. Hover one for the step. Show on the world map
  (setting) turns it off. With OpenMap, they show across its seamless map.
- Going back to a step the guide skipped (you had it already) shows its click-when-done lines ticked off; lines the
  game can check (an item equipped, a skill) show what's true.
- Clicking a line that uses or equips an item or casts a spell does just that, and says so when you hover it; it no
  longer sets the waypoint too.
- A line the game can check (a recipe you learn, an area you explore) no longer says "click when done".
- Guide lines can be optional (`:Optional()`): the step is done once its other lines are, and the optional one shows
  its own state, e.g. Equip Fishing Pole beside Reach Fishing 75.
- Guide lines can be ticked off by a condition (`:Done`), a Use line too: `s:Use(recipe):Done("knows 7751")` learns the
  recipe when clicked and is ticked once you know it; `s:Do("Buy ..."):Done(...)` stays in the list, ticked, once
  it holds.
- Guide conditions can test a profession's cap: `skillmax Cooking >= 225` (Expert learned).
- Guides can have exploration lines (`s:Explore(challenge, area)`), done once the game counts the area as found in that
  exploration challenge.
- Guides can list the parts of a bigger challenge still to finish (`s:Challenge(challenge, guide)`): each line goes once
  its part is finished, and clicking it opens that part's guide in a tab of its own.
- **Guide buttons in the legacy challenges window** (WoW Forever): a challenge a guide leads through gets a Guide
  button that opens it in a tab of its own. Guides say which challenge with `g.challenge = id`.
- Guides whose steps can be done in any order (`g.nearest = true`) go to the first stop on the shortest way from where
  you are through the steps left, planned again each time a step is done and when the guide is opened.
- A quest you can't take yet, because its chain began in a guide you skipped, is no longer asked for: its accept line
  is greyed out with what it needs under it ("Needs Blessed Arm"), and you go on with the arrow (The Legend of Stalvan
  in Duskwood, after doing dungeons instead). Needs QuestieDB, which knows each quest's pre-quests;
  for WoW Forever's new chains it doesn't know yet, a quest given where one of the same name is turned in follows that
  one, and the Menethil Statuette chain (A Friend of the Family, The Shamed Lieutenant) is known. Click the line
  (**Catch up**) for a catch-up guide to it. When the quest before it is still in your log, it says "Finish ... first"
  (The Night Watch). A turn-in for a quest you don't have shows the same way: "Not in your quest log". **Quests missing
  a prerequisite** in the settings can skip such steps when there's nothing else to do in them: always, or only when
  catching up isn't worth it; a quest still in your log keeps its step either way. Quests of the same name are told
  apart by their part: "The Night Watch (part 2)".
- **Skip hearthstone steps** (in the settings): leaves out the "Hearth to ..." and "Set your Hearthstone to ..." lines,
  and skips a step with nothing else to do. For when you would rather fly or walk, or keep your Hearthstone where it
  is.
- **Quest Catchup** works for any quest, from all the guides: click a greyed "needs ..." line, or type
  `/og catchup` with a quest's id, name or link. It takes the steps from the guides leading to yours first, then from
  any other guide that has them. Before, it found nothing to catch up on: it took every earlier quest for a
  breadcrumb. Next to Catch up it says whether it's worth it: its XP per minute (the quests it does, the quest and the
  rest of its chain; the way there and back counted) against the guide's own: **worth it**, **about even** or **not
  worth it**. Tick **Detailed catch-up numbers** in the settings for the numbers themselves ("5.4 bars, ~40 min, 0.8x
  this guide's XP per minute"). Behind the guide's pace (a quarter of a level or more short of where its level range
  says you should be by now), catching up is worth it: you'll need the XP anyway. Needs QuestieDB, which knows the XP.
- **Guide picker**: the gear beside the search is a menu now. The guides only for the other faction are left out;
  tick **Other faction's guides** there to list them too. **Settings** opens the settings as before.
- **Destroy cheapest item**, for full bags: finds the item in your bags worth the least at a vendor and asks before
  destroying it (Enter says yes). Grey items go first. Tools (Blacksmith Hammer, Mining Pick, fishing poles...), items
  a vendor won't buy and items the guide still needs are left alone. Bind a key
  in Key Bindings > Obvi Guide, or use the window's gear menu or `/og junk`.
- A finished side task now goes away whole: its notes and "kill these" lines no longer stay behind after it's done.
- Side tasks are set a little apart from each other, so you can tell where one ends and the next begins.
- Notes in side tasks look like the step's own notes (muted gold) rather than plain white lines.
- Clicking a line in the step sets the waypoint: to the line's own spot when it has one, else to the step's. A line
  that also targets or uses something still does that. Clicking again, or once you're there, leaves the waypoint as it
  is, so Shortest Path Forever isn't asked to plan the way anew each t

# Obvi Guide

## v0.4.0

- **Guide tabs**: several guides open at once, one shown. The title's menu lists them, with close buttons and Add guide.
- **Quest Catchup**: finds the earlier quests you skipped that the rest of the guide needs, and opens their steps as a
  short guide beside it that leads back when done. In the settings menu, or `/og catchup`. Needs QuestieDB.
- **Auto accept and turn in** only take the quests of the current and the next step; other quests are left alone.
- **Guide search** also lists the steps a quest or NPC is in, under its guide: click one to open the guide there.
- **Minimap dots** are coloured by what the step is about: red to kill, green for an NPC, blue to collect, purple to
  click.
- With Shortest Path Forever showing the way, the step's objective shows under its waypoint marker.
- Trainer and vendor lines tick off when you close the window.
- Flight paths you have are recognised more reliably.
- A quest line the game doesn't track (resurrecting Henze Faulk) no longer ticks off as soon as you take the quest.
- Quest chains whose quests share a title tick off properly when the game starts you further along the chain.
- Close buttons work in combat.
- Guide writers: `ObviGuide.AddFormat` and `ObviGuide.Toolkit` let other addons add guide formats.

## v0.3.1

- **Waypoint arrow**: Obvi Guide's own arrow points the way to the current step, with the objective and the distance.
  Settings > Waypoints picks how the way is shown instead: the arrow, Shortest Path Forever, TomTom, the map pin, or
  none.
- **Guide picker**: lists every guide; the ones not for your character are greyed out.
- **Profession steps**: guides can ask for a skill level ("Reach Mining 65") or a rank to train, and show the progress.
- **Flight paths**: "get the flight path" steps also tick off in zones with a map of their own.
- **Retail**: the step divider no longer shows as a bright bar.
- Guide writers: `ObviGuide.Load`, `ObviGuide.List` and `ObviGuide.Read` for tools like Obvi Guide: Scribe.

## v0.1.0

- First release.

    - ObviScribe -> ObviGuide\_Scribe, ObviGuides\_Dungeons ->

      the guides of your own installed Zygor addon to Obvi Guide in game.  
      Never released: not in the release workflow, left out of every zip.  
    - ObviGuide.Add declared in docs/api.lua

## [v0.2.0](https://github.com/rhnorskov/obvi-guide/tree/v0.2.0) (2026-11-02)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/rhnorskov/obvi-guide/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/rhnorskov/obvi-guide/releases)

- Monorepo: Scribe, guide packs, own waypoint arrow  
    The repo now holds one folder per addon, each released as its own  
    CurseForge project when its TOC has a project id:  
    - ObviGuide: the viewer (moved into its own folder)  
    - ObviScribe (Obvi Guide: Scribe): record, edit, test and export guides  
      in game; open any loaded guide as a draft; build guides by hand  
    - ObviGuides\_Dungeons: The Hall of Thanes and Ruins of Lordaeron  
    - ObviGuides\_Professions: Mining and Blacksmithing (after  
      wow-professions.com, with credit)  
    Viewer:  
    - own waypoint arrow (the minimap quest arrow, enlarged) and a  
      Waypoints setting: arrow, Shortest Path Forever, TomTom, map pin, none  
    - skill goals and conditions (Skill, Train, "skill Mining >= 75")  
    - flight paths found on the zone's own map and on new-path messages  
    - guide picker lists every guide, greys out ones not for this  
      character; flat folders, Zygor under Zygor\  
    - upcoming-step divider, ObviGuide.Load/List/Read for Scribe,  
      replace a guide added again with the same id  
- Guide picker, retail fixes, and more step actions  
    - Guide picker: a Finder-style column view in the quest log's look, with  
      search by title, folder, quest and NPC name, Recent guides, and a  
      resizable window. Opened from the window title, /og guides or a key.  
    - Retail Zygor guides: |gossip lines are instructions, |count N reads part  
      of an objective, objectives matched by text when numbered differently,  
      no auto-advancing during loading screens, flight path lines tick off once  
      the game lists the flight point as discovered.  
    - Action keys: one per mob, Interact for objects to click, and picking the  
      guide's dialogue option while an NPC's dialogue shows. Named Action  
      Button 1-4.  
    - Lines flash like the objective tracker when they turn done; a step done  
      in front of you stays a moment before moving on.  
    - Click the step counter to go to a step by number.  
    - Auto accept and turn in cover the whole guide's quests, on by default.  
    - Flip window: header at the bottom, growing upwards.  
- Read guides lazily; Zygor reader for retail  
    Guides from a format with a head step (Zygor) are listed at login and read when first opened. The Zygor reader resolves zones by client (Forever: classic names with the map shift; retail: Zygor's map table, then the client's maps) and handles more retail syntax (achievements, vehicles, allied races, newer classes). The guide menu nests groups by path.  
- Workflow: back to the packager's v2 tag  
- Workflow: actions/checkout v7, BigWigs packager v2.6.1
